key_insight: TRACE argues that long-horizon agents need turn-level credit assignment, not just final outcome scores. By estimating which tool-use turns actually contributed to success, it can reward useful intermediate actions even when the full trajectory fails.
problem_solved: The paper addresses sparse, noisy, and misleading supervision in multi-turn agent training, where outcome-only rewards become unreliable as tool-use trajectories grow longer and contain many intermediate decisions.
method: Assign rewards at the turn level instead of only at the end of the rollout.
Estimate credit for each action or tool call based on how much it moves the agent closer to the goal.
Use these credit estimates during post-training to better learn from partially successful or failed trajectories.
impact: This makes training long-horizon AI agents more stable and sample-efficient, especially for tool-using systems that perform complex multi-step tasks. Practitioners can learn from richer feedback than binary success/failure, improving performance on difficult real-world workflows.

paper_title: TRACE: Turn-level Reward Assignment via Credit Estimation for Long-Horizon Agents
paper_authors: Leitian Tao, Baolin Peng, Wenlin Yao, Tao Ge, Hao Cheng
